name: 2-7 Triple Draw
description: 2-7 Triple Draw (Deuce to Seven) is a lowball draw poker game where the lowest hand wins. Players get five cards and three drawing rounds to improve; straights and flushes count against you; aces are high. Best possible hand is 7-5-4-3-2 offsuit.

overview.description: 2-7 Triple Draw (Deuce to Seven) is a lowball draw poker game where the lowest hand wins. Players get five cards and three drawing rounds to improve; straights and flushes count against you; aces are high. Best possible hand is 7-5-4-3-2 offsuit.

history.origins: USA; lowball draw poker variant. Introduced at the World Series of Poker (WSOP) in 2004; featured in mixed-game formats.
timeline: Present: Common in mixed games and online poker
history.cultural: Popular among experienced poker players and in high-stakes mixed games.
history.evolution: Lowball variant of Five Card Draw with three draw rounds; influenced by Ace-to-Five Lowball.

setup.dealing: Five cards each; three draw rounds (discard and replace) with betting between each.

rules.objective: Make the lowest possible five-card hand. Win the pot at showdown.
rules.gameplay: Five cards each; betting then draw (discard and replace), betting, draw, betting, draw, betting, showdown. Three draws; stand pat or draw 0-5 cards each time.

strategy.basic: Play tight: start with hands that have a deuce and a seven, or three cards to an eight that don’t make a straight. Never draw to hands that can make a straight. A-2-3-4-5 is bad (ace is high). Best hand is 7-5-4-3-2 offsuit.
strategy.intermediate: Position matters: act last when possible to see opponents’ draw sizes. Be aggressive—bet and raise more than you check and call. From early position raise only with strong two-card draws (e.g. 2-3-4, 2-3-7); loosen in late position.
strategy.advanced: Snowing: in position, stand pat with weak hands when opponents have drawn many cards to pressure them. On the final draw, jack-high is slightly favoured over a one-card draw; adjust by position. Avoid drawing to nine-lows when inexperienced.
tips: Best hand is 7-5-4-3-2 (no flush, no straight); aces are always high.
Starting hands: need a deuce and seven or three to an eight; avoid straight draws.
Snowing (standing pat with a bluff) works when opponents have drawn and you act last.
Position is critical—see how many cards opponents draw before deciding.
